P1.evidence: An application exists and was referenced, but only 35 minutes in and as a rhetorical confirmation — 'That's also something you put in your application, right?' — not read back at the open to make the prospect feel seen. The frame was two-thirds delivered: 'first of all, go into where you're at at the moment, where you want to go, see if we can help you bridge that gap' — where you are and where you want to go are there, what's in the way is implied by 'bridge that gap', and what you need is absent. No agreement was sought; the rep answered his own frame with 'Yeah, we can, perfect.' The open question landed cleanly: 'What can we potentially help you with that?'

P2.evidence: Age, height and weight were all asked ('So you're 39. How much do you weigh at the moment?' and height given as 1.77m), though the weight answer is garbled in the recording and the rep did not re-ask. Occupation was confirmed but the desk-bound question was never put — the prospect volunteered 'I'm being sit down, I sit down, I work on my computer all the time.' Health conditions, own or hereditary, were never asked at any point in a 63-minute call. Injuries were never asked either; the rep asked only about mobility — 'Do you feel like you have just complete free range of motion, or do you have somewhat of stiffnesses that come up?' — which surfaced the hips but not injury history or duration. Training week, results and diet were all run properly and in depth. Sleep is the significant miss: the prospect raised it himself at 00:37:22 with 'I haven't mentioned, though, there's one thing I was thinking about is sleep. I don't sleep enough. And I know that's a big problem' — the rep had not asked, which scores as a miss, and he then converted it straight into a benefit claim rather than a baseline fact. Energy was only reached obliquely through 'the feel better aspect... Is that like mental feel like energy wise?'

P3.evidence: Aesthetics were worked well — the rep pushed past 'a better body' to body fat percentage, to chest and arms, and landed the athletic-build distinction ('You want to have an athlete build, it sounds like'). The bridge ran cleanly: 'I'm very curious about like the feel better aspect... What is that to you?' The deep question was asked twice and rephrased when the prospect did not follow. But 'who else does that impact' was never asked — the child came up unprompted ('I want my kid to see me doing sports. So he's proud of his dad') and the rep then supplied the meaning himself rather than drawing it out: 'It's more so for yourself and also to be a good role model, it sounds like, for your kids.' The prospect answered 'Yeah, exactly' and the thread was dropped rather than driven into identity or legacy. The recap was factual ('the goal is for you to get abs, less fat, run a chest') with no 'this isn't really about the weight' reframe. Nothing physical he wants to do but cannot was ever asked.

P4.evidence: The strongest phase of the call. The rep asked 'how long have you now done your own program for?' and got the full history — one year of Body Pump, six months of boxing with an in-person coach, tennis, occasional gym. He asked why it did not stick and the prospect named it himself: 'because I haven't found a coach, and I haven't found the program that is great for me.' The root-cause question was direct — 'what do you think is, like, the missing piece that we need to solve?' — and produced the gap in the prospect's own words: 'having a coach that is behind you.' P4f scores as a miss on the strict rule: the prospect arrived at 'it's not even a matter of knowledge... the fact of having someone behind you has a huge consequence on the result' entirely unprompted, and the rep only confirmed it afterwards ('more of like an accountability aspect'). Credit the outcome, not the ask. What happened with each past attempt was thin — the Body Pump and boxing endings were skated over.

P5.evidence: Not run. In 63 minutes there is no two-year question, no 'are you willing to settle for that', no 'why not' and no line in the sand. The nearest approach is 'life is going to get probably even more busy. And when a newborn gets a little bit older, then maybe something else happens again' — which the rep used to justify needing a portable system, not to make the cost of inaction real. The prospect handed him the material for it unprompted ('I've been wanting to have it since a long time... I was like, okay, later, later, later') and it was not picked up. This is the second consecutive Richard Claessen call in this batch with Phase 5 entirely absent.

P6.evidence: The pre-presentation commitment work was about effort rather than belief: 'are you willing to also put in that effort if Trevor is in your back pushing you?' and 'if you can promise that to yourself, then know that we can fit in there', closed with 'I don't know if you agree with those thoughts' and a clean 'Yeah, no, I actually agree, of course.' That is a real yes but to the wrong question. The belief question proper came only after the three pillars — 'do you feel like if we get those three things... in place that you're going to be able to get to the goals' — answered 'Yeah, of course, yeah.' The 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in' question was never asked, which matters enormously here: the answer would have surfaced the documentation blocker before the price rather than 20 minutes after it.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted — price presented at 00:39:45, next steps described ('We get started. We do the investment rights. Then we book a meeting with Trevor. I think either tomorrow or on Monday'), and the rep pushed for a decision ('So what do you say?'). No payment was collected. P11c is scored a miss rather than N/A because the agreement was actively discussed and the rep's handling of it is what stalled the call: he stated the contract is generated only post-payment and that he has no access to it — 'I don't have a site into the contract, it gets sent when we've done the payment' and 'I can't just open a new one, like, it's all automatic'. The prospect asked for it four separate times. Onboarding scheduling and the welcome-email steps were never reachable.

objection_plays.detail: The certainty move ran almost verbatim — 'So is it that you just want to have certainty? That if you do start with this, it is actually what I've just told you it is.' — and the prospect confirmed 'Yes.' The rep also improvised an analogy in the spirit of the BRIDGE and PLANE moves, using a car purchase, but it backfired: the prospect took the analogy and turned it against him ('if I pay on the time I see the car... I'm going to fall in love by making decisions based on my feelings, not based on my reason. So that's why I take 15 minutes just to see what's written'). None of the remaining moves ran — no pleasure-versus-pain question, no burned-before frame, no 'how will you know if you never actually try'. Having correctly diagnosed certainty as the need, the rep then tried to satisfy it with social proof rather than with the written evidence the prospect had asked for.

Trigger is explicit — 'in six months, it's a bit actually pricey... it's almost 900 per month.' The rep skipped isolation entirely and went to a worth question that is not in the play ('Is it for you worth 6,000 or 5.2 in order to get fitter and feel better?'), which happened to work — 'Yeah, of course. It's worth it.' The upfront-versus-plan move ran but only reactively, after the prospect asked about payment options, and it was delivered as a discouragement rather than an option: 'Most guys, put it up front... If needed, we can split it up, but we don't have anything set usually for that.' Zero of the six financial-picture moves ran. Defensible in this case — money was demonstrably not the blocker — but the play was not run.

Script gap, and the one that decided this call. The prospect's objection was documentary, not emotional: he wanted to read what he was buying before paying, and to see the agreement before payment rather than after. He said so at least five times across 20 minutes, in plain terms — 'I want something written where it says, what's the plan', 'I want to always want to take the time to read it calmly and alone', 'you send me the contract, I read'. There is no play for this in the playbook, and no asset behind the play either: the rep's own words were 'we don't have anything that we send to people' and 'this is the only thing that we've written down'. What he did send was an outdated internal document he immediately had to disclaim — 'I do see that it misses the one-on-one aspect a little bit' — which strengthened rather than resolved the objection. This is a company-asset gap, not a rep failure, and it should be escalated as such.

Second script gap: a prospect who sells the same way. 'Because I'm in the business of digital products. I know sometimes in closing, we can oversell or we can do stuff' and 'now we have a process where we do it in a two times closing. Because our products is more expensive than you guys.' He is a high-ticket seller with his own closers, is explicitly aware of the frame being run on him, and told the rep that his own company sells over two calls at this price point. Nothing in the playbook covers a peer buyer, and the rep continued running the standard single-call structure. A scripted two-call path for this profile is the obvious missing asset and the prospect himself named it.

'So what do you say?' / 'I'm thinking... Yeah. I'm not sure. I think it's great. But at the same time, yeah, I'm wondering.' No OA move ran against this. The rep replied only 'You're wondering?' and then followed the prospect into the price calculation. The core moves — 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', the identity question — were all available and none were used.

notes: Discovery and root cause were genuinely good; this call was not lost on the process, it was lost on a missing asset. A price-insensitive, in-ICP, high-intent buyer asked five times for something written and the company had nothing to give him. Escalate that above the coaching. The rep-level coaching points are the two structural repeats: Phase 5 was skipped again, and the 'any reason you wouldn't go all in' question would have surfaced the documentation blocker before the price rather than 20 minutes after it. Also worth correcting: 'we don't have anything set' for payment plans contradicts what the same rep quoted on another call the same day.
